articles.title: Personal data (definition)
articles.summary: Information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.

articles.title: Sensitive personal data (definition)
articles.summary: Racial or ethnic origin, religious belief, political opinion, union or religious, philosophical or political membership, health, sex life, genetic or biometric data linked to a person.

articles.title: Data protection impact report (RIPD)
articles.summary: Controller documentation describing processing that may risk civil liberties and fundamental rights, with the measures, safeguards and risk mitigation mechanisms adopted.

articles.title: Purpose principle
articles.summary: Processing serves legitimate, specific, explicit purposes informed to the data subject, with no later processing that is incompatible with them.

articles.title: Adequacy principle
articles.summary: Processing must be compatible with the purposes informed to the data subject, according to the context of the processing.

articles.title: Necessity principle
articles.summary: Processing is limited to the minimum needed for its purposes, covering only relevant, proportionate and non-excessive data.

articles.title: Security principle
articles.summary: Technical and administrative measures protect personal data from unauthorised access and from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, communication or dissemination.

articles.title: Legal bases for processing
articles.summary: Lists the ten legal bases for processing personal data, from consent to credit protection; item VIII covers health protection by health professionals or health services.

articles.title: Legal bases for sensitive data
articles.summary: Sensitive data may be processed with specific, prominent consent or, without consent, only in the listed cases such as legal duty, life protection or health protection.

articles.title: Children's and adolescents' data
articles.summary: Processing the data of children and adolescents must serve their best interest.

articles.title: Parental consent for children's data
articles.summary: Processing a child's data requires specific and prominent consent from at least one parent or legal guardian.

articles.title: End of processing
articles.summary: Processing ends when its purpose is reached, the data are no longer needed, the data subject withdraws consent, or the authority orders it.

articles.title: Deletion after processing ends
articles.summary: Data are deleted after processing ends, except for legal duty, research, permitted transfer to a third party, or anonymised use by the controller.

articles.title: Data subject rights
articles.summary: The data subject may obtain confirmation, access, correction, anonymisation or deletion, portability, information on sharing and revocation of consent.

articles.title: International transfer
articles.summary: International transfer of personal data is allowed only in the listed cases, such as adequate countries, contractual guarantees, consent or authorisation by the authority.

articles.title: Transfer with guarantees
articles.summary: Transfer is allowed when the controller offers and proves guarantees: specific clauses, standard clauses, global corporate rules, seals, certificates or codes of conduct.

articles.title: Transfer with consent
articles.summary: Transfer is allowed with the data subject's specific and prominent consent, after prior information on the international nature of the operation.

articles.title: Assessment of the foreign protection level
articles.summary: The authority assesses the level of data protection of the foreign country or organisation, weighing legislation, the nature of the data, safeguards and other circumstances.

articles.title: Standard and specific clauses
articles.summary: The authority defines the content of standard contractual clauses and verifies specific clauses, global corporate rules, seals and certificates.

articles.title: Changes in guarantees
articles.summary: Changes to the guarantees presented for an international transfer must be communicated to the authority.

articles.title: Record of processing operations
articles.summary: Controller and operator keep a record of the processing operations they carry out, especially when based on legitimate interest.

articles.title: Impact report on request
articles.summary: The authority may order the controller to prepare a data protection impact report, including for sensitive data, under its regulation.

articles.title: Minimum content of the impact report
articles.summary: The report describes the data collected, the methodology for collection and information security, and the controller's analysis of safeguards and risk mitigation.

articles.title: Data protection officer
articles.summary: The controller appoints an officer (encarregado) and publicly discloses the officer's identity and contact details.

articles.title: Security measures
articles.summary: Controllers and operators adopt technical and administrative measures to protect personal data from unauthorised access and from accidental or unlawful incidents.

articles.title: Incident communication
articles.summary: The controller notifies the authority and the data subject of a security incident that may cause relevant risk or damage.

articles.title: Simple fine
articles.summary: Administrative sanction: a simple fine of up to 2% of the revenue in Brazil in the last fiscal year, capped at R$ 50,000,000.00 per infraction.
